ended: Lost the East 1st Round 3-4 to CLE

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (defense-first breakthrough)
archetype.definition: A team that went from 30-52 to a 46-win, top-five defense and a winning record, then lost a seven-game first round it was good enough to win, without the offense or rebounding to close it out.

report.headline: Toronto's defense delivered the turnaround; a thin offense and the glass ended it

recap.finish: 46-36, third in the Atlantic; lost the East 1st Round 3-4 to CLE
recap.body:
This was a defense with an offense attached. Toronto finished 5th in defensive rating at 113.0, against a league average of 115.7, while the offense sat 15th, essentially on the league line. The defense rested on two things: forcing mistakes (opponents turned it over at a 14.3 rate, 4th) and running shooters off the line (opponents hit 34.9% from three, 3rd). It was hardest on small forwards, holding them to among the fewest points of any defense. After 30-52 and 25-57 the two years before, that turned a lottery team into a playoff team in one season.

The season had one great month and a lot of solid ones. A 2-4 October gave way to a 12-3 November, built on a nine-game winning streak, that put them at 14-7. December was the low point at 6-8. After that they never collapsed, since the longest losing streak all year was four, and they ground out winning months in January, February and April around a 7-8 March. They finished strong: in the last ten games they outscored opponents by 12.2 a game, well above their season margin. The point differential implied 48 wins, so 46-36 reflects the team's quality honestly, if anything slightly short of it.

Scottie Barnes drove it. He ranked 3rd among 93 at his position and made the All-Star and All-Defensive Second teams, with a 4.2 BPM and 7.8 Win Shares that led the team. The frontcourt graded A- and earned it beyond Barnes: Sandro Mamukelashvili scored at a 63.7 TS % and added 6.2 Win Shares, and Collin Murray-Boyles and Jakob Poeltl gave quality minutes. Brandon Ingram led the team with 1,655 points and made the All-Star team, but the team was 5.9 points per 100 worse with him on the floor. RJ Barrett, playing the same position, posted a positive on-off. The wings' A- grade rests more on volume than on impact.

The weak spots were structural. The backcourt graded C. Immanuel Quickley was solid, but Jamal Shead's 444 assists came with a 49.1 TS %. As a team Toronto took threes at one of the lowest rates in the league, 25th at 36.3%, and made them at a below-average 35.4%. That left an offense that didn't turn over the ball but rarely created easy points. Rebounding was middling to poor: 23rd in rebounds a game and below average on the boards overall.

Against Cleveland those weaknesses decided it. Toronto dropped the first two on the road, held serve at home with a 22-point win and a 93-89 grinder, lost Game 5 by five, then forced Game 7 with a 112-110 overtime win. They lost Game 7 away, 114-102. The defense still forced turnovers, ranking 2nd among playoff teams, but Toronto grabbed only 69.2% of the available defensive rebounds, 15th of 16, and finished the series 12 points behind. Barnes was excellent, with an 8.1 BPM, and Murray-Boyles shot 68.5 TS %. Ingram played five of the seven games at a 44.0 TS %, and Quickley has no postseason line in the sheet.

highlights.title: A top-five defense built on disruption
highlights.body: Toronto finished 5th in defensive rating by forcing turnovers and taking away the three, a big change from defenses that ranked 17th and 25th the previous two years. That kind of defense comes from scheme and personnel rather than shooting luck. Barnes's All-Defensive season sits at the center of it, so it should carry over.

highlights.title: Barnes became a true centerpiece
highlights.body: Barnes ranked 3rd among 93 at his position, led the team in Win Shares, and raised his game in the playoffs with an 8.1 BPM. He was the one Raptor who clearly outplayed Cleveland. The team will be built around him.

highlights.title: Deep, efficient frontcourt
highlights.body: The frontcourt graded A- and was efficient up and down the rotation. Mamukelashvili spaced the floor at a 63.7 TS %, and Murray-Boyles was the second-best Raptor in the playoffs. It is the deepest group on the roster.

lowlights.title: A backcourt and offense without punch
lowlights.body: The backcourt graded C, and its highest-minutes playmaker after Quickley shot a 49.1 TS %. Combined with one of the league's lowest three-point attempt rates, the offense finished dead average. That is the ceiling on this team until the guard spots or the shot profile change.

lowlights.title: Losing the glass when it counted
lowlights.body: Rebounding was below average all year, and in the playoffs it got worse: Toronto was second-to-last among playoff teams in defensive rebounding. A defense that forces misses and turnovers gave Cleveland second chances, and that cost Toronto a series it lost by just 12 points over seven games.

lowlights.title: Ingram's volume, not impact
lowlights.body: Ingram scored the most points on the team at a 26.9 usage rate, but the team was worse with him on the floor. In the playoffs he shot a 44.0 TS % and is now listed out. The A- wing grade overstates how much he moved the needle.

arc.note: After a 2-4 start and a 12-3 November surge, the Raptors settled into a long run of modestly winning months, with December the only real dip. They closed with their best margin of the year over the last ten games.

recap.nextYear: Most of this carries over. The 46 wins were earned, not lucky: the differential implied 48. The defense and the frontcourt are real, and both run through Barnes, with Mamukelashvili and Murray-Boyles as efficient support. The work is in the backcourt, which graded C and lacked shooting, and in the shot diet, since few teams took fewer threes. Rebounding is the other repair, and the playoffs showed how costly it can be. The open question is the wing scoring: Ingram carried the volume but not the on-court results, while Barrett's numbers looked more like winning ones. How that resolves decides whether this defense finally gets an offense to match.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus a seven-game series, with a margin that matches the record
